title: Emotion, Prosody, and Articulation
header: Thursday 1 October 2026 - 09:00-11:00 - Long Oral 12 - Emotion, Prosody, and Articulation [Cross-area long papers Oral session]

items.title: ProSarc: Prosody-Aware Sarcasm Recognition Framework via Temporal Prosodic Incongruity
items.authors: Prathamjyot Singh(Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology); Ashima Sood(Ulster University); Sahil Sharma(Ulster University); Jasmeet Singh(Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology)
items.abstract: We present ProSarc, an audio-only framework that detects sarcasm by modelling temporal prosodic incongruity, that is, the mismatch between local prosodic dynamics and the utterance-level emotional baseline. Dual encoding paths, a Global Emotion Encoder and a Temporal Prosody Encoder (BiLSTM + multi-head attention), feed a Prosodic Incongruity Analyzer that produces a scalar incongruity score for classification. Monte Carlo dropout provides uncertainty estimates, and an attention-based mechanism localises sarcastic onset without frame-level labels. ProSarc outperforms prior audio-only methods on MUStARD++ (F1 = 75.3) and generalises to spontaneous (PodSarc, F1 = 62.9) and cross-lingual speech (MuSaG, F1 = 65.6). Ten-run validation confirms the contribution of incongruity modelling (Wilcoxon p=0.002, Cohen's d=1.51). Human evaluation shows that model uncertainty tracks perceptual ambiguity and predicted onsets align with human-annotated temporal windows.

items.title: A Two-Stage Defence for Robust Federated Speech Emotion Recognition
items.authors: Yi Chang(Imperial College London); Sofiane Laridi(Leibniz University Hannover); Zhao Ren(University of Bremen); Gregory Palmer(Leibniz University Hannover); Björn W. Schuller(Imperial College London); Marco Fisichella(Leibniz University Hannover)
items.abstract: With machine learning and speech processing advancements, speech emotion recognition has gained popularity recently. However, speech data cannot be protected when it is uploaded and processed on servers in the internet-of-things applications of speech emotion recognition. Further, deep neural networks have proven to be vulnerable to human-indistinguishable adversarial perturbations. The adversarial attacks generated from the perturbations may result in deep neural networks wrongly predicting the emotional states. We propose a novel federated adversarial learning framework for protecting both data and deep neural networks. The proposed framework consists of i) federated learning for data privacy, and ii) adversarial training at the training stage and randomisation at the testing stage for model robustness. The experiments show our proposed framework effectively protects speech data locally and improve model robustness against a series of adversarial attacks.

items.title: Segregate, Refine, Integrate: Decomposing Multimodal Fusion for Sentiment Analysis
items.authors: Alexios Filippakopoulos(National Technical University of Athens; Synaptic Bloom); Elias Kallioras(National Technical University of Athens); Nikolaos Xiros(National Technical University of Athens; Athena Research Center); Efthymios Georgiou(National Technical University of Athens; University of Bern); Alexandros Potamianos(National Technical University of Athens; Archimedes AI; Synaptic Bloom)
items.abstract: Multimodal fusion must simultaneously refine modality-specific signals and model cross-modal interactions; two competing objectives typically entangled within the same operation. We propose SeRIn (Segregate, Refine, Integrate), a multimodal LM fusion scheme that enforces this separation as an architectural prior. Modality-specific representations evolve along isolated pathways, each refined against its respective encoder context, while a dedicated cross-modal pathway accumulates their joint evolution without contaminating unimodal streams. Full cross-modal interaction is deferred to a final prediction step — ablations confirm that structured interactions, not added capacity, drive the gains; gate analysis under visual corruption reveals emergent modality reweighting without explicit supervision. SeRIn achieves state-of-the-art results on CH-SIMS and CMU-MOSEI, improving all metrics on both benchmarks.

items.title: An Acoustic Landmark Database of the English Lexicon via Articulatory Synthesis
items.authors: Mateo Cámara(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid; MIT); José Luis Blanco(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid); Juan Ignacio Godino-Llorente(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid); Jeung-Yoon Choi(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid); Stefanie Shattuck-Hufnagel(MIT)
items.abstract: Acoustic landmark theory treats speech as organized around the acoustic consequences of articulatory gestures that shape the vocal tract and airflow. Progress is limited by the scarcity of large, unambiguously annotated landmark datasets. We invert the problem by generating speech from landmark patterns. Using the Pink Trombone physical vocal-tract synthesizer, we produce an English lexicon for two adult configurations (male, female). With direct control of gestures, we place landmark labels algorithmically at the exact times of their physical events (e.g., oral closures/releases). The corpus contains >200,000 synthesized words, rendered for both configurations with time-aligned annotations; intelligibility is measured with STOI. We leverage it for statistics across the lexicon from an articulatory-event view, reporting landmark frequencies and dominant cue patterns, and enabling quantitative studies plus training/benchmarking of automatic landmark detectors.

items.title: NewAppVoice: Tools for Visualizing and Correcting Acoustic Measures
items.authors: Amélie Elmerich(CNRS & Sorbonne Nouvelle); Yao Dong(CNRS); Louise McKeever(CNRS & Sorbonne Nouvelle); Katia Chirkova(CNRS); Lise Crevier-Buchman(CNRS & Sorbonne Nouvelle; Université Paris Saclay); Claire Pillot-Loiseau(CNRS & Sorbonne Nouvelle); Angelique Amelot(CNRS & Sorbonne Nouvelle)
items.abstract: Phonetic analysis of little-studied languages, particularly those with complex segmental inventories or typologically rare features, often requires extensive manual verification of acoustic measurements. In the absence of established reference formant values, automatic extraction frequently produces systematic errors that must be visually inspected and corrected. Most large-scale scripts process datasets without interactive feedback, limiting transparency and reproducibility when manual intervention is necessary. This study presents NewAppVoice, a reproducible workflow integrating multiple formant-calculation algorithms with synchronized visualization of signals and measurements. Unlike fully automated pipelines, the software combines algorithmic processing with structured manual verification, improving reliability while ensuring transparency. The software and derived applications are freely available as open access tools supporting reproducible research on under-documented languages.
